o1.biggest_strength: Puts the real numbers (10 notes, 5-12 cards, 10/14 mm) and honest trade-offs in calm brand voice right above the fold, and handles the break-in and cash returns head-on.
o1.biggest_mistake: Buries the return-cutting line under the button and gives the buyer no obvious next step for the 'too much cash' case, and the assumptions section loads the owner with follow-up questions rather than confidence.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Move the break-in and cash-capacity reassurance into the line under the add-to-cart button, add a single graceful 'pick a bigger wallet if you carry a lot of cash' link beside the bullets, and trim the assumptions to one line.

o2.biggest_strength: Same honest numbers and brand voice, but adds a 'browse our other wallets' escape hatch for the cash-heavy buyer, puts the return-cutting line right under the button, and gives the owner a simple way to check it worked with today's figures.
o2.biggest_mistake: The 'how to tell it worked' section and link block edge toward strategy notes rather than page copy, and the subtitle repeats the opening line almost exactly as Output 1, so less differentiation on the very top line.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Keep the measurement plan as a separate short note rather than inside the deliverable, and sharpen the subtitle so it leads with the slim number or the proof line instead of a straight spec list.

reason: Both are usable, honest and on-brand with the right numbers; Output 2 nudges ahead because it gives the cash-heavy buyer somewhere to go, places the return-cutting line where the buyer decides, and hands me a simple way to check it worked.
